instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: The codes of planning or intending are H2803I (to plan, devise, mean), H2803J (to think, plan), H1819 (to imagine, think) and H5452 (to think, intend). The lexicon bears out devising and purpose, in Isa 10:7, Jer 23:27, Dan 7:25, Num 33:56, 1Sa 18:25 and Job 6:26.
observations.grounds: to plan, devise, mean

observations.text: The codes of giving thought are H2803I and H2803J (to think, account), H2142 (to remember, call to mind), H0995 (to discern, consider), H1819 (to imagine, think), H6245B (to think), G3049 (to count, consider), G3421 (to remember, fix the thoughts upon), G3539 (to understand, reflect), G1760 (to reflect on) and G1761 (reflection). H1931 (he) is a pronoun in a unit. The lexicon bears out attention of the mind turned to a matter or person, as in Phili 4:8, Heb 11:15, Lam 1:9 and Mat 9:4.
observations.grounds: to remember, recall, call to mind

observations.text: The codes of reckoning something as so are G3049 (to credit, count, reckon), G2233 (to think, consider, count), G2919 (to decide, consider) and H2803J (to think, account). G1161 (but) is a connective in a unit. The lexicon bears out a judgment that counts a thing as of a kind, in Rom 14:14, Gen 38:15, Act 26:8 and the others.
observations.grounds: to credit, count, reckon

observations.text: The code of being minded is G5426 (to think, regard, hold an opinion; to set one's mind on; to have a certain attitude). The lexicon bears out a set of mind, in Rom 12:3, Phili 3:15 and 1Cor 13:11.
observations.grounds: to have a (certain) attitude

observations.text: The codes of thoughts as purposes are H4284 (thought, device; plan, purpose), H4209 (purpose, device, plot) and H1902H (meditation, plotting). The lexicon bears out purpose and device, placed by the verses in the heart, as in Gen 6:5 and 1Ch 28:9.
observations.grounds: device, plan, purpose

observations.text: The codes of thoughts that arise and are held are G1261 (reasoning, thought), G1270 (thought), G1271 (mind, thinking), G1761 (reflection), G3540 (mind, thought; scheme, design), H4093 (knowledge, thought; place of knowledge), H5587B (disquietings), H6248 (thought, idea), H7454 (purpose, thought), H7476 (thought), H7808 (thought), H8312 (disquieting thoughts) and H2808 (reasoning). H1697G and H1697I (word, thing), H1961 (to be) and G3588 (the) stand in the units. The lexicon bears out thoughts as what the mind holds, some of them disquieting, as in 1Cor 2:11, 2Cor 10:5, Amo 4:13 and Dan 2:29.
observations.grounds: disquieting thoughts, thoughts

observations.text: The codes of supposing something to be so are G1380 (to think, imagine, suppose, presume), G3543 (to suppose, presume, expect), G3633 (to think, suppose, presume), H0559 (to say in one's heart, to think), H1819 (to imagine, think) and H7200H (to see, consider). The lexicon bears out a belief held, which the verses test, as in 1Cor 3:18, 1Cor 10:12 and 1Cor 14:37.
observations.grounds: to suppose, presume, expect

observations.text: The surface conceive carries codes of bodily conceiving in Num 5:28, Num 11:12, Judg 13:3, Judg 13:5, Judg 13:7, Psa 51:5, Isa 7:14, Mat 1:23, Luk 1:31 and Heb 11:11: H2232, H2029, H2030A, H3179, G4815, and the Greek phrases of G1722 with G2192 and of G2602 with G4690G. Each is a woman becoming pregnant or a person conceived, with no act of thought.
observations.grounds: you shall conceive and bear a son

observations.text: In Job 15:35, Isa 33:11 and Isa 59:4 the same code H2029 is turned to what a person forms within: trouble, chaff and mischief are conceived and evil, stubble and iniquity are born. The figure of the womb is the verses' way of naming a thought formed and brought out in act.
observations.grounds: They conceive trouble and give birth to evil

observations.text: The surface opinion carries H1843 in Job 32:6, Job 32:10 and Job 32:17, knowledge or a judgment that Elihu holds back and then declares, and H3820A in Pro 18:2, the heart, where the fool's opinion is what his heart holds. In these four it is a view a person holds and speaks.
observations.grounds: let me also declare my opinion

observations.text: In Mat 22:16 and Mar 12:14 opinion carries G0991, to see or look at: Jesus does not look at a person's standing. No view is held; the English word renders a phrase of not regarding the face.
observations.grounds: we know that you are true

observations.text: In Num 36:6, 2Sa 10:3, 1Ch 19:3, Jer 40:4 and Jer 40:5 think carries H5869I, the eye, or H0413 with it, in the idiom of what is good in someone's eyes: the think is a person's own judgment of what is best or fitting.
observations.grounds: Let them marry whom they think best

observations.text: In 2Ki 18:20, Isa 36:5, 2Ch 13:8 and Eze 11:5 think carries H0559, to say, in its sense of saying in one's heart: the thought is a view put into words, and in Eze 11:5 the Lord states what the house of Israel thinks.
observations.grounds: So you think, O house of Israel

observations.text: Think carries the Hebrew and Aramaic verbs of reckoning and devising: H2803J in Job 6:26, Job 35:2, Job 41:32, Psa 119:59, Psa 144:3 and Jer 23:27, H2803I in Isa 10:7, H1819 in Est 4:13 and H5452 in Dan 7:25. In some the thought is a judgment held, in others a plan pursued.
observations.grounds: When I think on my ways

observations.text: In 2Sa 18:27 think carries H7200H, to see or consider: the watchman judges from what he sees. In Psa 119:52 it carries H2142, to remember: thinking of the rules from of old is calling them to mind.
observations.grounds: When I think of your rules from of old

observations.text: Think carries G1380, to think or consider, in most of the Gospel verses and in 1Cor 4:9, 1Cor 7:40, 1Cor 12:23, 2Cor 11:16 and Heb 10:29: a view held about what is so, often asked of the hearer (Mat 17:25, Mat 22:42, Luk 10:36) or corrected (Mat 26:53, Luk 12:51, Luk 13:2, Joh 5:45).
observations.grounds: What do you think about the Christ

observations.text: Think carries G3543, to suppose or deem, in Mat 5:17, Mat 10:34, Act 17:29 and 1Cor 7:26: in the first three the view is forbidden (do not think, we ought not to think), in 1Cor 7:26 Paul gives his own judgment.
observations.grounds: Do not think that I have come

observations.text: Think carries G1760, to reflect, in Mat 9:4, G3539, to understand or perceive, in Eph 3:20, and G3049, to count or consider, in 2Cor 12:6 and Phili 4:8: the mind turned to a matter, evil in the heart in Mat 9:4 and what is excellent in Phili 4:8.
observations.grounds: Why do you think evil in your hearts

observations.text: In Rom 12:3 and Phili 3:15 think carries G5426, to be minded, twice in each verse: a set of mind, sober rating of oneself, maturity. In 2Pe 1:13 it carries G2233, to consider, with G1161, a connective.
observations.grounds: not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think

observations.text: In Gen 32:8, 1Sa 27:11, 1Sa 27:12, 2Sa 5:6, 2Ki 7:12, 2Ch 32:1, Neh 6:9 and Psa 64:5 thinking carries H0559, to say, and the quoted sentence that follows gives the thought as inner speech: Jacob's plan for the camps, David's fear of report, Achish's trust, the enemies' hope that the work will stop. In Neh 6:9 H0853 is the object marker in the unit.
observations.grounds: Their hands will drop from the work

observations.text: In Rom 1:21, 1Cor 14:20 and 1Pe 4:1 thinking is the mind's way of working: G1261 reasoning that became futile (with G2532, and), G5424 understanding to be mature and not childish, G1771 the attitude to arm oneself with.
observations.grounds: arm yourselves with the same way of thinking

observations.text: In 2Cor 12:19 thinking carries G1380, a view held all along, in Phili 1:17 G3633, an intent to afflict, and in Heb 11:15 G3421, being mindful of the land they left.
observations.grounds: If they had been thinking of that land

observations.text: The surface thinks carries H0559 in 1Sa 20:3, Saul's inner speech that David quotes, and in the New Testament G1380 in Luk 8:18, 1Cor 3:18, 1Cor 10:12, 1Cor 14:37, Gal 6:3, Phili 3:4 and Jam 1:26, G3049 in Rom 14:14 and G3543 in 1Cor 7:36. In most of the Greek verses it is a view of oneself that the verse tests: wise, standing, a prophet, something, religious.
observations.grounds: if anyone thinks he is something

observations.text: In the narratives and sayings of Gen 20:11, Gen 26:9, Gen 31:31, Gen 32:20, Exo 2:14, Jos 22:28, Judg 3:24, Judg 15:2, Rut 4:4, 1Sa 16:6, 1Sa 18:11, 1Sa 18:17, 1Sa 18:21, 1Sa 20:26, 2Sa 14:15, 2Sa 14:17, 2Sa 21:16, 2Ki 5:11, 2Ki 20:19, Job 29:18, Psa 94:18, Isa 39:8, Jer 3:7, Jer 3:19 and Eze 20:32 thought carries H0559, to say, and the thought is given as the quoted words a person said within. Small words of the units are H3588A in Gen 20:11 and H0834A in Eze 20:32.
observations.grounds: I thought that you would take your daughters

observations.text: Thought carries Hebrew verbs of reckoning, devising, likening, remembering and discerning: H2803J in Gen 38:15 and Psa 73:16, H2803I in 1Sa 18:25 and Psa 40:17, H1819 in Num 33:56, Psa 48:9 and Psa 50:21, H5869I in 2Sa 3:19, H2142 in Lam 1:9, H0995 in Pro 14:15 and Pro 21:29 (with H1931). The thought is a judgment, a plan, a likening or attention given.
observations.grounds: the prudent gives thought to his steps

observations.text: Thought as a noun of what the mind holds: H1697G with H1961 in Deu 15:9 (an unworthy word in the heart), H4284 in 1Ch 28:9 (every plan and thought the Lord understands), H6248 in Job 12:5, H2808 in Ecc 9:10, H7808 in Amo 4:13. In Jon 1:6 H6245B is the god giving a thought, with H0194 perhaps; in Mic 2:8 H7725G is turning back, not a thought.
observations.grounds: an unworthy thought in your heart

observations.text: In the Gospels and Acts thought carries G1380 (Mar 6:49, Luk 24:37, Joh 11:13, Joh 13:29, Act 12:9), G3543 (Mat 20:10, Act 8:20) and G2919 (Act 26:8): a view taken of what is so, which the verse shows mistaken or in question. In Luk 12:17 it carries G1260 with G3004G, the rich man reasoning to himself.
observations.grounds: they thought it was a ghost

observations.text: In 1Cor 13:11 thought carries G5426, the child's mindedness; in 2Cor 9:5 and Phili 2:25 G2233, a judgment of what is necessary; in 2Cor 10:5 G3540, every thought taken captive; in 1Ti 3:7 G3141, a good report from outsiders, not a thought.
observations.grounds: take every thought captive to obey Christ

observations.text: In Psa 40:5, Psa 92:5, Isa 55:8, Isa 55:9 and Mic 4:12 thoughts carries H4284, purposes and plans, and in Psa 139:17 H7454: here the thoughts are the Lord's own, many, deep, precious, higher than man's and unknown to the nations.
observations.grounds: my thoughts are not your thoughts

observations.text: In Gen 6:5, 1Ch 29:18, Job 21:27, Psa 56:5, Psa 94:11, Pro 12:5, Pro 15:26, Isa 55:7, Isa 59:7, Isa 66:18 and Jer 4:14 thoughts carries H4284, purposes and devices of people, most of them evil and known to the Lord; in Psa 10:4 H4209, the wicked man's purposes, and in Lam 3:62 H1902H, the musing of the assailants.
observations.grounds: every intention of the thoughts of his heart

observations.text: Thoughts carries H5587B, disquietings, in Job 20:2, H7454 in Psa 139:2, H8312, anxious thoughts, in Psa 139:23, H4093, the place of knowledge, in Ecc 10:20, and H1697I, things, in Eze 38:10: what rises and is held within, known to God.
observations.grounds: Try me and know my thoughts

observations.text: In Dan 2:29, Dan 2:30, Dan 4:19, Dan 5:6, Dan 5:10 and Dan 7:28 thoughts carries the Aramaic H7476: thoughts that come in the night or alarm the one who has them.
observations.grounds: his thoughts alarmed him

observations.text: In the New Testament thoughts carries G1761 in Mat 9:4, Mat 12:25 and Heb 4:12, G1261 in Mat 15:19, Mar 7:21, Luk 2:35, Luk 5:22, Luk 6:8, 1Cor 3:20 and Jam 2:4, G1270 in Luk 11:17, G1271 in Luk 1:51, G3540 in 2Cor 11:3, and G3588, the article, in 1Cor 2:11: reasonings and designs of the heart, known by Jesus, by the Lord and by a person's own spirit.
observations.grounds: out of the heart come evil thoughts

observations.text: A negator reaches the thinking itself in Mat 5:17, Mat 10:34, Joh 5:45, Act 17:29, Rom 12:3, 2Cor 11:16, Isa 10:7 and Lam 1:9: do not think, we ought not to think, let no one think, his heart does not so think, she took no thought. The view is forbidden or denied.
observations.grounds: Do not think that I have come

observations.text: In Jos 22:28, 1Sa 20:26, 2Sa 5:6, Psa 10:4, Isa 55:8, Mic 4:12, Mat 6:7, Mat 22:16, Luk 12:51, Act 12:9, Rom 1:21, Jam 1:26 and the other verses of this group the negator stands in the quoted thought, in the content supposed, or on another verb of the sentence (know, honor, bridle, care, heap up, delay): it does not reach the thinking. Adjacency is not scope.
observations.grounds: the wicked does not seek him

observations.text: Qualifiers give the moral quality of the thoughts: evil in Gen 6:5, Psa 56:5, Psa 64:5, Isa 59:7, Eze 38:10, Mat 9:4, Mat 15:19 and Mar 7:21; righteous against wicked in Pro 12:5 and Pro 15:26, upright in Pro 21:29, prudent in Pro 14:15, proud in Luk 1:51, futile in 1Cor 3:20, at ease in Job 12:5; in Phili 4:8 what is true, honorable, just and pure is what to think on, and in Heb 4:12 the word discerns the thoughts.
observations.grounds: every intention of the thoughts of his heart was only evil

observations.text: Where thinking is a judgment, the qualifier gives the value judged: best in Num 36:6, good in 2Sa 3:19, 2Sa 18:27, Isa 39:8, Jer 40:4 and 1Cor 7:26, right in Jer 40:5 and 2Pe 1:13, necessary in Phili 2:25, incredible in Act 26:8, last in 1Cor 4:9, worse in Luk 13:2, Luk 13:4 and Heb 10:29, wise in 1Cor 3:18, spiritual in 1Cor 14:37, less honorable in 1Cor 12:23, more in Mat 20:10 and Phili 3:4, unclean in Rom 14:14. In Psa 40:5, Psa 92:5 and Dan 7:28 many, very and greatly measure the thoughts; in 1Cor 13:11 and Phili 3:15 child and mature name the mindedness.
observations.grounds: Let them marry whom they think best

observations.text: In Gen 20:11, Gen 32:20, Judg 15:2, 1Sa 16:6, 2Ki 7:12, Isa 36:5, Dan 5:6, Luk 12:17, Joh 16:2, 1Cor 10:12, Eph 3:20 and the other verses of this group the qualifiers describe persons, places or acts around the thought (there, behind, younger, surely, hungry, alive, mere words, then, nowhere, whoever, lest, all): none qualifies the thinking itself.
observations.grounds: no fear of God at all in this place

observations.text: The Lord or God is named as the one who knows, searches or has thoughts: he sees the thoughts of man in Gen 6:5, knows them in Psa 94:11 and 1Cor 3:20, searches and knows them in Psa 139:23 and 1Ch 28:9, declares them in Amo 4:13 and Eze 11:5; his own thoughts are many and deep in Psa 40:5 and Psa 92:5, precious in Psa 139:17, above man's in Isa 55:8 and unknown in Mic 4:12; he takes thought for the poor in Psa 40:17 and Psa 144:3.
observations.grounds: knows the thoughts of man

observations.text: Jesus is named as the one who knows the thoughts of others in Mat 9:4, Mat 12:25, Luk 5:22 and Luk 6:8, and as the one who asks the hearer's thought in Mat 17:25 and Mat 22:42; in Joh 11:13, Joh 11:56 and Joh 13:29 others think about him and mistake his meaning; in Mat 22:16 and Mar 12:14 he is said not to regard appearances, and in Joh 5:45 Moses is named as the accuser.
observations.grounds: But Jesus, knowing their thoughts
